52.description: The committee recommends amending the Vehicles for Hire Bylaw, addressing taxi payment terminals, van fare calculations, and driver safety.

chips.text: Recommended
Administration's van rate calculation focused on $14,000 capital cost, not operating costs.
Councillor Block questioned the discrepancy in vehicle purchase prices in the report appendix.
Taxi union president Malik Draz disagreed with proposed payment machine and van rate amendments.
Councillor Dubois could not support van rate changes, citing unaddressed higher operating costs.
Administration will report back on options to improve driver safety by September 2026.

53.description: Saskatoon approved new criteria to prioritize where sidewalks and cycling facilities will be built, guiding future active transportation infrastructure development.

chips.text: Approved
9 for, 0 against
Administration confirmed using judgment to prioritize projects beyond strict scoring.
New cycling facility prioritization criteria were established for the first time.
Walking Saskatoon raised concerns about criteria implementation and federal funding delays.
New prioritization criteria include an explicit equity component for sidewalk projects.

58.description: The city will rehabilitate Archibald Arena, exempting it from high-performance building standards due to its age and budget priorities. This project aims to extend the arena's life by 15-20 years.

chips.text: Approved
9 for, 0 against
Council inquired about the $9.8 million federal funding application.
Saskatoon residents using Archibald Arena for ice sports and dryline activities.
The timeline for federal funding approval for the project remains unknown.
Administration committed to presenting alternative funding options if federal application fails.
